Steps:
1. Re-read the deliverable files in their entirety.
2. Re-verify all dates and calculations from scratch (independently if possible).
3. Cross-check all citations against library/INDEX.md.
4. Verify that all facts used exist in the documents.
5. Check for inconsistencies.

Let's be rigorous. Things to re-check:

- Day-of-week claims: 2026-11-19 Thursday (PDF states "quinta-feira" — confirm), 2026-12-10 Thursday (PDF states "quinta-feira" — confirm). Other day-of-week notations in the memoria: 2026-11-23 Monday, 24 Tuesday, 2026-12-15 Tuesday, 2026-12-11 Friday, 2026-12-14 Monday, 2026-12-18 Friday, 2027-01-21 Thursday, 2027-02-03 Wednesday, 2027-01-25 Monday, 2027-02-05 Friday. Verify all with Python.
- Cross-check holiday claims against the calendar file: 2026-11-20 (Friday) listed as "sex" in calendar — confirm: yes, line 24 states "20/11/2026 (sex)." 2026-12-08 (Tuesday) "ter" — yes. 2027-01-01 Friday — yes. 2027-01-25 Monday Capital only — yes. 2027-02-08/09 Carnival Mon/Tue — yes.
- Counting rules: publication = next business day after posting (Lei 11.419 art. 4 §3, CPC 224 §2). Citation: 2026-11-19 (Thu) posted; next business day: 11-20 is holiday, weekend, 11-23 Monday = publication date. Start = first business day after publication = 11-24 Tuesday. ✓
- Answer (contestacao): 15-day deadline under art. 335 III via art. 231 VII. Count from 11-24 as business day 1 (224: exclude the start date, include the deadline date — standard counting treats start date as day 1... wait. Art. 224: "excluindo o dia do começo e incluindo o dia do vencimento (excluding the start date and including the deadline date)." Hmm — this is the classical computation rule: the deadline starts running from the start date, excluding the start date from the count... In fact, under this rule, if the start (dia do começo) is day X, the count is X+1...? Let me think carefully.

Two frameworks:
(a) CPC 231: the "dia do começo do prazo (start date of the deadline)" is the publication date (art. 231 VII). Art. 224: exclude the start date, include the deadline date. So if publication = the start date, the first day counted = publication + 1 business day... and the deadline date is the 15th day counted.
(b) CPC 224 §3 + Lei 11.419 §4: "A contagem do prazo terá início no primeiro dia útil que seguir ao da publicação (the deadline count begins on the first business day following publication)" — the count begins on the first business day after publication. So the count starts from that day: is the start date itself counted as day 1?

These two frameworks must be reconciled. Standard Brazilian practice: publication on date P; day 1 of the deadline = the first business day after P. So the 15th business day after P (counting business days, skipping the first day) = deadline. Under framework (a) with 231: start = P, exclude P, count from the next day — same result. Under framework (b): count begins the day after P, and that day counts as day 1. Same result: day 1 = first business day after P.

In my calculation: publication 11-23 Monday; day 1 = 11-24 Tuesday; day 15 = 12-15. ✓ Consistent under both frameworks.

For the judgment (sentença): publication 12-11 Friday; day 1 = 12-14 Monday. ✓.

However — in the JSON, "inicio_contagem": "2026-11-24" is listed, and I counted 11-24 as day 1. This is consistent with the art. 224 §3 / §4 framework. Good.

- Verify 15 business days from 11-24: script gave 12-15; re-verify: November 24, 25, 26, 27 = 4; November 30, December 1, 2, 3, 4 = 9; December 7 = 10; December 9 = 11 (skipping December 8 holiday); December 10, 11 = 13; December 14, 15 = 15. ✓
- Embargos (motions for clarification) 5 days: December 14, 15, 16, 17, 18 = 5 → 12-18 Friday ✓.
- Appeal: 5 days completed by 12-18; suspended December 20–January 20; resumes January 21; remaining 10: January 21, 22 (7), January 25, 26, 27, 28, 29 (12), February 1, 2, 3 (15). ✓ 2027-02-03.

Confirming 2027-01-21 is Thursday: 2027-01-01 Friday (+20 days) → 20 + ... let me just trust Python. But wait — is January 21 a business day? Not on the holiday list. ✓. And is the recesso (recess) inclusive of 01-20? Yes ("inclusive" — calendar note + art. 220 "inclusive").

- Day-of-week labels for counted days in the memoria table: 2026-11-24 Tuesday, 25 Wednesday, 26 Thursday, 27 Friday, 11-30 Monday, 12-01 Tuesday, 02 Wednesday, 03 Thursday, 04 Friday, 07 Monday, 09 Wednesday, 10 Thursday, 11 Friday, 14 Monday, 15 Tuesday ✓ (confirm with Python).
- Judgment table: 12-14 Monday ... 12-18 Friday ✓; 01-21 Thursday, 22 Friday, 25 Monday, 26 Tuesday, 27 Wednesday, 28 Thursday, 29 Friday, 02-01 Monday, 02 Tuesday, 03 Wednesday ✓.
- Note about art. 224 §1: "se coincidirem com dia em que o expediente forense for encerrado antes... (if they coincide with a day when court business was concluded before...)" — I noted there were no such circumstances. But note: the calendar mentions 2026-11-18 (Ash Wednesday, no business until noon) — unrelated, posting was 11-19. Also 12-24/31 have no business — inside the recesso anyway. OK.

Hmm, wait, one more subtle issue: the calendar states "18/02/2026 (Wed) Ash Wednesday (no business until 12:00 — TJSP: no deadline)." Irrelevant to our dates (February 2026 is before this). No problem.

- Art. 229 §1 claim: "Cessa a contagem em dobro se, havendo apenas 2 réus, é oferecida defesa por apenas um deles. (The double-counting ceases if, there being only 2 defendants, a defense is offered by only one of them.)" I wrote "the double deadline could be extinguished mid-deadline" — accurate enough as a supplementary argument.

- Potential error: the memoria's source section states "anotação sobre art. 1.026 (note regarding art. 1.026)" — library's cpc_prazos_recursais.md states "§… a oposição de embargos interrompe o prazo para a interposição de recurso (art. 1.026) (filing of embargos interrupts the deadline for filing an appeal (art. 1.026))." So the library attributes the interruption to art. 1.026, but the citation listed is "CPC arts. 335, 1.003 §5º, 1.023." When citing "arts. 1.023/1.026" — art. 1.026 is not in the INDEX.md citation column, though it is mentioned within the library file itself. The contract says "all citations must point to a file in library/INDEX.md." Citing the file that covers it, and referring to "art. 1.026 mentioned within the art. 1.023 annotation in the same file," would be safer. Let me check how the deliverable phrases it. STATUS item 1: "a apelação é interrompida (CPC arts. 1.023/1.026, anotação da biblioteca) (the appeal is interrupted)" — it says "anotação da biblioteca (library annotation)," which is defensible: the source is cpc_prazos_recursais.md which is in the INDEX. Memoria §7: "Pela anotação da biblioteca (CPC, arts. 1.023/1.026) (per the library annotation)" — likewise. I could make explicit: "conforme anotação no arquivo library/cpc_prazos_recursais.md (referindo-se ao art. 1.026) (per the annotation in file library/cpc_prazos_recursais.md (referring to art. 1.026))." Also, the text of the interruption rule has that garbled "§…" — the annotation is part of the library file, no problem, but should note that the INDEX does not list art. 1.026 — worth flagging as a minor caveat rather than changing the substance. Refine the wording to point to the file, and flag it in the "pontos em aberto/ressalvas (open items/caveats)."

- Another check: the citation intimation is a "citação/intimação (service of process notice/summons)" — service through the attorney on the record ("na pessoa de seu advogado constituído (through the retained attorney)"). Under art. 335, the term for the answer is... Art. 335 III: "prevista no art. 231, de acordo com o modo como foi feita a citação (as provided in art. 231, according to how the service of process was carried out)." Art. 231 VII: publication date when summoned via official gazette. This is exactly what the library covers. No problem. The library's art. 335 excerpt says "...III – prevista no art. 231" with ellipsis — the original art. 335 enumerates items I (mediation), II (order...), III (art. 231). Since the library excerpt itself uses "…," it's permissible.

- The memoria's §5 arithmetic "prova real (proof)": from November 24 to December 15 = 22 days: November 24–30 is 7 days; December 1–15 is 15 days; total 22 ✓. Weekends: November 28, 29, December 5, 6, 12, 13 = 6 ✓. Holiday: December 8 = 1 ✓. 22 − 7 = 15 ✓.

Non-deadline days: December 19, 20, 26, 27 (weekends, 4 days); December 21–25... let me just verify the suspension period: December 20–January 20 is entirely non-running = 32 days; plus weekend days outside the suspension: December 19, 26, 27 (December 26–27 are within suspension anyway), January 23–24, 30–31 (4 days), February... let me recount: 52 total − 32 suspension days = 20 days in the active window (December 14–19 = 6; January 21–February 3 = 14 → 20 ✓).
